abstract: Primary mediastinal seminoma is an uncommon neoplasm, the optimal management of which is still debated. Radiotherapy produces a 65% disease-free survival rate. We assess whether these results have been improved with the advent of cisplatin-based chemotherapy. Data from 14 patients treated at the Institut Gustave-Roussy were reviewed. 9 had received cisplatin-based chemotherapy (Group 1): their outcome was compared with that of 5 patients treated with radiotherapy without chemotherapy (Group 2). We also reviewed data from the English literature using strict criteria, and report results concerning patients who received cisplatin-based chemotherapy and those who received radiotherapy. 8 of the 9 patients (89%) in Group 1 are long-term disease-free survivors and only 3 of 5 patients in Group 2. The patient who died in Group 1 was the only one who refused surgical resection of residual masses after chemotherapy. The review of the literature revealed that 59 of 68 (87%) patients initially managed with cisplatin- or carboplatin-based chemotherapy and for whom sufficient data are available, are long-term survivors and free of disease. Some of these patients had also received radiotherapy. Only 64 of 103 (62%) treated with thoracic radiotherapy without chemotherapy were long-term disease-free survivors. The disease-free survival rate of 51 patients who received cisplatin-based chemotherapy (excluding those who received carboplatin) was 86%. The difference in survival between patients administered cisplatin-based chemotherapy and those who underwent radiotherapy is apparently not due to unbalanced prognostic factors, the effect of time or non-specific medical management. We conclude that cisplatin-based chemotherapy allows long-term disease-free survival in approximately 85% of patients. These results seem to be higher than those obtained without cisplatin-based chemotherapy. However, a randomised study is required for definitive conclusions, but it is very unlikely that such a study will be performed due to the rarity of this neoplasm. Another alternative would be a meta-analysis based on individual data.
abstract_ja: 原発性縦隔セミノーマは稀な腫瘍であり、その最適な治療は依然として議論がある。放射線療法では無病生存率は65%である。シスプラチン併用化学療法の登場により、これらの成績が改善したかを評価した。Institut Gustave-Roussyで治療された14例のデータを検討した。9例がシスプラチン併用化学療法を受けた（群1）。これらの転帰を、化学療法を行わず放射線療法のみを受けた5例（群2）と比較した。さらに、厳格な基準を用いて英語文献のデータも検討し、シスプラチン併用化学療法を受けた症例と放射線療法を受けた症例の結果を報告する。群1の9例中8例（89%）が長期無病生存者であり、群2では5例中3例のみだった。群1で死亡した1例は、化学療法後の残存腫瘤の外科的切除を拒否した唯一の患者だった。文献的検討では、シスプラチンまたはカルボプラチン併用化学療法を初期に受け、十分なデータがある68例中59例（87%）が長期生存かつ無病であった。これらの一部は放射線療法も受けていた。化学療法を行わず胸部放射線療法のみを受けた103例中、長期無病生存者は64例（62%）のみであった。シスプラチン併用化学療法を受けた51例（カルボプラチンを除く）の無病生存率は86%であった。シスプラチン併用化学療法を受けた患者と放射線療法を受けた患者の生存差は、予後因子の不均衡、時間の経過、非特異的な内科的管理によるものとは考えにくい。シスプラチン併用化学療法により、約85%の患者で長期無病生存が得られると結論する。これらの成績は、シスプラチン併用化学療法を行わない場合より高いようである。ただし確定的な結論にはランダム化比較試験が必要であり、本腫瘍の希少性のため実施はきわめて困難と思われる。別の方法として、個々の患者データに基づくメタ解析が考えられる。
